articles.headline: Intuitive Surgical: The Long Road to Everyday Surgery
articles.summary: MBI Deep Dives offers a comprehensive long-form analysis of Intuitive Surgical (ISRG), tracing its origin from a government-funded robotics lab through its IPO, the elimination of rival Computer Motion, the prostatectomy adoption decade, and the 2013 gynecology controversy. The piece examines how the da Vinci installed base generates three distinct recurring revenue streams and what the company's push toward routine 'everyday surgery' — including high-volume, cost-sensitive procedures like cholecystectomy — means for long-term procedure penetration and revenue inflection. Competitive dynamics from Medtronic Hugo and J&J Ottava are addressed alongside Intuitive's ~40% non-GAAP operating margins and 84% recurring revenue at ~$12B in 2025 revenue.
articles.why_it_matters: For investors sizing a long-term position in surgical robotics, this piece provides the durable moat analysis — patent estate consolidation, installed base lock-in, and procedure penetration curves — needed to assess ISRG's compounding runway against emerging competitors.
